label_provenance.review_scope: whether the quoted public-source evidence directly supports AND/OR among the supplied same-scope child events
label_provenance.rule: AND requires direct evidence all supplied child events must co-occur; OR requires direct evidence that any one supplied child or path is sufficient; co-listed possible causes or co-occurring states alone remain unknown.
label_provenance.review_note: Exploratory AI role review performed before model inference. Not human domain-expert sign-off, not a second-agent review, and not project Gold.

inference_input_policy: The model receives only parent event, direct child event texts, and the exact transcribed source-scope evidence. Source identity, document metadata, expected labels, reviewer notes, and expected gate evidence are withheld.
scope_note: Incremental external-source probe adding paraphrased direct AND/OR evidence and two conjunction near-misses. This is a smoke-test extension, not a representative benchmark, calibration set, or production policy test.

gate_nodes.parent_event: System failure or accident occurs by the specified critical path.
gate_nodes.parent_evidence: The source identifies the system failure or accident as the top event.
gate_nodes.candidate_set_evidence: Resistor 1 must fail in Mode A and Resistor 2 must fail in Mode B in order for the system failure or accident to occur.
gate_nodes.expected_gate_evidence: Resistor 1 must fail in Mode A and Resistor 2 must fail in Mode B in order for the system failure or accident to occur.
gate_nodes.label_rationale: The source says both supplied failures must occur for the parent event by this critical path; this is a different explicit formulation from a 'both ... must occur' prose template.

gate_nodes.parent_evidence: The source describes a system fault-tree gate whose output is event k.
gate_nodes.candidate_set_heading: System fault-tree gate inputs m through z
gate_nodes.candidate_set_evidence: all events m thru z must occur (fail)
gate_nodes.expected_gate_evidence: all events m thru z must occur (fail)
gate_nodes.label_rationale: The rule explicitly requires every supplied event m through z to occur before event k occurs; the children enumerate the full stated range.

gate_nodes.parent_evidence: The source describes a system fault-tree gate whose output is event k.
gate_nodes.candidate_set_heading: Alternative system fault-tree inputs m through z
gate_nodes.candidate_set_evidence: if any of the events m thru z occur (fail), event k occurs
gate_nodes.expected_gate_evidence: if any of the events m thru z occur (fail)
gate_nodes.label_rationale: The source says any one of the supplied alternative failures produces event k, directly supporting OR. This is paired with an all-inputs-required case from the same manual; the two samples share one source cluster.

gate_nodes.parent_evidence: The source defines the event produced by a logic operation as its output event.
gate_nodes.candidate_set_evidence: A logical operation where the coexistence of all input events is required to produce the output event.
gate_nodes.expected_gate_evidence: A logical operation where the coexistence of all input events is required to produce the output event.
gate_nodes.label_rationale: The definition requires all input events to coexist to produce the output, directly expressing AND semantics without relying on the words 'AND gate'.

gate_nodes.parent_event: Precise tracking of water movement in the closed plant-growth chambers is inconsistent.
gate_nodes.parent_evidence: The source says the system's precise and accurate tracking of water movement is not consistent.
gate_nodes.candidate_set_heading: Possible causes of inconsistent water tracking
gate_nodes.candidate_set_evidence: Possible causes include hardware errors, undetected vapor loss from chamber leakage, and unmeasured changes in water volume in the plant growth trays.
children: Undetected vapor loss from chamber leakage.
Unmeasured changes in water volume in the plant growth trays.
gate_nodes.label_rationale: The abstract lists possible causes and joins the final list item with 'and', but does not say each cause alone is sufficient or all causes must coexist.

gate_nodes.parent_evidence: The transcript recounts a probable sequence ending in tank rupture.
gate_nodes.candidate_set_evidence: This in turn caused the pressure and a temperature within the tank to increase. The tank then ruptured.
gate_nodes.label_rationale: The narrative states that pressure and temperature increased before rupture, but it does not state that both supplied states are individually necessary or jointly sufficient children of the rupture event. Co-occurrence and sequence do not by themselves establish an AND gate.

limitations: This extension has six nodes from five source documents; two gate labels share the same CARE III manual and therefore are not independent source clusters.
Several positive controls are explanatory gate definitions rather than independently validated real-system fault trees; they test text interpretation, not domain fault-tree completeness.
The possible-cause-list sample uses the official NASA NTRS abstract because that record exposes no downloadable PDF.
The Apollo 13 near-miss is intentionally conservative: the quoted chronology reports two co-occurring states before rupture, not a proof that the physical mechanism had no Boolean relation.
Labels were assigned by the primary AI role reviewer before model inference; they are not human expert Gold or independent second-agent findings.
Model self-reported scores are uncalibrated and cannot be interpreted as event probabilities or used as production thresholds.
This extension does not test source-document extraction, cause completeness, recursive tree generation, formal gate-policy selection, database integration, or production readiness.
